comparison: Perfect agreement on promoter mapping and SNP identification (C4, C41-C47, C81, C84). Both evaluations find the allele-specific expression analysis, luciferase reporter assays, promoter swap experiments, and site-directed mutagenesis convincing. Reviewers explicitly acknowledged the mapping to ~1kb fragment and SNP7 identification without concerns.

Perfect agreement on binding affinity data (C6, C52-C60, C73-C79). Both evaluations accept the EMSA experiments showing quantitative Kd differences and the loss of preferential tandem binding in mutant CLOCK. Reviewers implicitly accepted these findings as part of their positive evaluation without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on USF1 identification and functional validation (C3, C29-C34, C36-C37). Both evaluations find the expression analysis, transgenic rescue experiments, and molecular characterization convincing. Reviewers explicitly praised the identification of USF1 through transcript analysis and transgenic validation. OpenEval also includes C35 (qPCR data) which peer review addresses separately.

Agreement on genetic mapping and behavioral phenotyping (C1, C19, C20). Both evaluations accept the semidominant inheritance pattern and statistical analysis. Peer review also covers QTL mapping claims (C2, C21, C22, C26) and subspecific origin analysis (C24, C25, C27, C28) in this result, which OpenEval separates into R2 and R3.

Agreement on QTL mapping and congenic analysis (C2, C21, C22, C26). Reviewers explicitly praised the 'clever combination of QTL and haplotype block mapping' that narrowed the region to ~900 Kb. Both evaluations find the mapping resolution and validation convincing.

Agreement on subspecific origin analysis and ancestral allele identification (C23-C28). Both evaluations accept the correlation between subspecific origin and suppressor phenotype. Peer review groups this with other mapping claims, while OpenEval treats it as a separate result.

Agreement on competitive binding demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR (C5, C48-C51, C82). Both evaluations accept the reciprocal binding patterns at E-box sites. Peer review groups this with ChIP-Seq data (C61-C67, C86) which OpenEval separates into R9, and acknowledges shared DNA-binding specificity without challenging the core findings.

Agreement on genome-wide ChIP-Seq analysis (C7, C61-C67). Both evaluations accept the increased overlap between USF1 and CLOCK:BMAL1 binding sites in mutant animals. Reviewers noted minor methodological concern about using homozygous versus heterozygous mice but did not challenge the core finding of shared DNA-binding specificity.

Disagreement on mechanistic model (C8, C68, C80, C85). OpenEval finds the integrated model well-supported by converging evidence, though notes 'partial agonist' characterization is inferential. Peer reviewers find the model ideal but state 'no direct proof is offered' for the chromatin structure maintenance claim, requesting DNase hypersensitivity experiments or removal of the claim.

Disagreement on USF1 knockout interpretation (C39, C40). OpenEval finds the knockout data supportive of a role in circadian amplitude regulation, noting context-dependency. Peer reviewers express concern about alternate interpretations and request cell-autonomous experiments and testing in Clock mutant background, stating this is 'critical in resolving the role of USF family of proteins.'

Agreement on elevated circadian gene expression (C35). OpenEval finds qPCR data from liver tissue convincing with highly significant p-values. Peer review implicitly accepts this as part of their positive evaluation of USF1 functional characterization without raising concerns.

Agreement on transgenic sufficiency (C38). Both evaluations accept that transgenic USF1 overexpression demonstrates genetic sufficiency for suppression. Reviewers explicitly noted the transgenic rescue without concerns, though they separately questioned knockout interpretation (C39, C40).

Agreement on discovery of interface between transcriptional networks (C83, C86). Both evaluations accept the ChIP-Seq evidence for extensive overlap in binding sites. Peer review acknowledges shared DNA-binding specificity as a key finding without challenging the novelty claim.

OpenEval evaluated background/literature claims (C9-C17, C23, C69-C72) as supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not assess established background knowledge.

OpenEval rated speculative claims about implications and future directions (C18, C87) as uncertain due to lack of direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not specifically address these forward-looking statements.
